label: 2nd/3rd copy-phase output in long sequences, token-gated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), almost entirely on the steps that output original tokens 1 and 2 (recall_idx 1-2, 89% of mass), i.e. the two steps right after <DEL>. The rate rises steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 59% of mass; L<=5 is near zero). It never fires in the original phase and essentially never at the delimiter or on the first copy output. Within those steps it depends on token identity: higher rates when the input is a/i/y or the output is s/f/j/i/r/b. Top activations are mostly inputs a/y/r/n at recall_idx 1-2 with L=9. Position alone (recall 1-2) gets mass recall 0.89 but precision 0.05; adding L and the token sets raises precision to about 0.23. The token dependence is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: a, i, y, s, r, g; least: h, 3, 2, z) and the token being output (most: s, f, j, i, b, r; least: m, w, -, o); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, recall_idx=2, t=10.
